text:
SPIKEWATCH round 2 — the user (verbatim) asked "how is the v8 gc always 0?" and it's the right question. Two real gaps to close. Do NOT commit yet.

GAP 1 — the GC bucket is VALUE-AMBIGUOUS, the same sin we just removed from the label. `GC 0us` can't be told apart from "callback never fired." Fix:
- Expose a GC INVOCATION COUNT from the shim (e.g. rjit_v8_gc_take_count) alongside the time. The callback increments it per prologue/epilogue pair.
- Keep SUB-MICROSECOND resolution — rjit_v8_gc_take_us does accum_ns/1000 (integer), so a sub-µs scavenge floors to 0. Report ns or µs-with-decimal so a real tiny GC shows as e.g. "0.7µs", not "0us".
- The attribution line must show BOTH: "V8 GC 0.7µs (scavenge ×3)" vs "V8 GC — (×0, never fired)". After this, "GC 0" is never ambiguous: it's either "fired N times, tiny" or "fired 0 times, binding dead."

GAP 2 — we are only ever seeing RECOVERED frames, never the actual spike frame. Every live line is tagged "SPIKE IN HOST TAPE — worst frame already recovered before owner counters were sampled; do not attribute stale counter deltas." So the buckets are sampled AFTER the spike frame passed — useless for catching what fires during a movement rubber-band. Fix:
- LATCH the per-bucket counters (GC us+count+type, present/vsync us, bridge us, unattributed us) per-frame so that when a spike frame is detected, the report shows THAT frame's latched buckets — not the current post-recovery frame's stale deltas.
- The whole point is: user moves the player → it rubber-bands → the spike line names the real cause for the BAD frame. If the host-tape architecture makes per-frame latching genuinely impossible, STOP and report exactly why (don't fake it) — but first try latching the bucket snapshot at the same point the tape captures the worst-frame phase data.

VERIFY before reporting: confirm the GC callback actually FIRES — the count must be > 0 in a running session with allocation (if it's 0, the mangled-symbol registration silently failed and THAT is the real bug to chase: wrong isolate handle, wrong mangled name, or callbacks not invoked). Don't report "done" with a 0 fire-count unexplained.

REPORT BACK: the shim's new count/resolution API, how you latched the spike-frame buckets, and — if you can get a build/run — a sample spike line showing GC fire-count. Note that the user must rebuild+restart the dev host to see it live (Zig/framework changes don't hot-reload); do NOT touch pane 6.

Stay in your own context — no Task tool, no subagents. tools/rjit only, ast-check not full build. No reset/revert. Commit only on my word.
resolution: Closed both spikewatch gaps from 'how is the v8 gc always 0?'. GAP 1 (value-ambiguity): the GC shim now exposes invocation COUNT (rjit_v8_gc_take_count) and NANOSECOND resolution (rjit_v8_gc_take_ns, replacing the floor-to-µs take_us) — a sub-µs scavenge reads '700ns ×3 (scavenge)', and a true zero reads 'V8 GC — (×0, never fired)', so 0 is never ambiguous. Wired gc_ns+gc_count through telemetry.Snapshot/CollectArgs → __tel_frame. GAP 2 (recovered-frame sampling): added __tel_frame_at(n) returning a historical snapshot from the host ring (which already latches per-frame buckets); both spikewatches now find the WORST frame by matching its total time (drift-tolerant: host ~240Hz vs JS ~60Hz) and report THAT frame's latched gc/present/bridge, labeled 'SPIKE FRAME CAUGHT (latched from host ring)', instead of the post-recovery current frame. The !countersReliable path now still names measured causes (GC/present/bridge) since boundary timers are independent of the stale owner counters. VERIFIED THE BINDING FIRES: extended v8_hello smoke target with a GC probe under heavy allocation → 'count=41 ns=6113239 last_type=1 PASS' (also pinned v8_hello to ReleaseFast — a Debug V8 binary hits the known lld CREL .init_array launch crash). telemetry suite 36/36 incl. new latch + sub-µs + count tests; perfWatch bundles; all Zig ast-checks clean. NOT committed (user's word). Dev host needs rebuild+restart to see it live; did NOT touch pane 6.
